sanskrit: imau pādau pra harāmy ā gṛhebhyaḥ svastaye | indraḥ paścād indraḥ purastād indro naḥ pātu madhyataḥ ||
english: I stride forward with these two feet, homeward for well-being. Indra behind, Indra before — may Indra guard us in the middle.

sanskrit: indro bhayaṃ vy asyatu śūdrāc ca na āryāc ca | indraḥ pathibhir adravad asamṛddhā aghāyavaḥ ||
english: May Indra cast away fear from us — from the Śūdra and from the Ārya alike. May Indra run down upon the roads those malevolent ones who have not prospered.

sanskrit: indro haniṣyatāṃ vadhaṃ vi naḥ pāśām̐ ivācṛtat ||
english: May Indra strike down the blow and disentangle our snares as though loosening fetters.

sanskrit: emaṃ panthām arukṣāma sugaṃ svastivāhanam | yena viśvāḥ pari dviṣo vṛṇakti vindate vasv āstam ety anāhataḥ ||
english: We have mounted this path, easy to travel, bearing well-being — by which one wards off all enemies, wins wealth, comes home uninjured.

sanskrit: parā vrajatu kṛntaty avakāṃ vikṣaṇann iva | viṣvañco yantv ?asyapālā viṣvañcaḥ paripanthinaḥ | viṣvak punarbhuvā mano asamṛddhā aghāyavaḥ ||
english: Let the cutting one go away, the one who strikes downward, as if slashing apart. Let the road-guards scatter in all directions, let the lurking highwaymen scatter in all directions. Let the minds of the malevolent, those who recur again and again, scatter in all directions — those who have not prospered.

sanskrit: svasty anv acākaśaṃ svasti praty acākaśam | svasti pathiṣu dhanvasu svasty apsv antaḥ | parivrajan svarita svastyayanam asi | bhāradvājaṃ svasti punarāyaṇam ||
english: I have looked forth with well-being, I have looked back with well-being. Well-being on the roads and deserts, well-being in the waters within. O wanderer, you whose sound is svara — you are the going-forth for well-being. O Bhāradvāja, may there be a safe return.

sanskrit: ya uttarād ājāyate madhugho madhughād adhi | vedāhaṃ tasmin bheṣajaṃ jihvā madhumatī mama ||
english: That which is born from the north, the madhugha plant, born from the madhugha — in it I know the remedy. My tongue is full of sweetness.

sanskrit: madhumat te parṇam āsa madhuśṛṅgota puṣpakam | madhumān parvatāsitha yato jāyasa oṣadhe ||
english: Sweet is your leaf, O plant, sweet your horns and your blossom. Sweet was the mountain from which you were born, O herb.

sanskrit: garbho asy oṣadhīnām apāṃ garbha utāsitha | atho somasya bhrātāsi madhugha prāva me vacaḥ ||
english: You are the embryo of the plants, and you were the embryo of the waters. Moreover, you are the brother of Soma — O madhugha, promote my speech.

sanskrit: śunam ahaṃ madhughasya pitur nāmeva jagrabha | yo mā hiraṇyavarcasaṃ kṛṇavat pūruṣapriyam ||
english: For good fortune I have grasped the name of the madhugha plant as one grasps a father's name — may it make me brilliant as gold, beloved of men.

sanskrit: priyaṃ mā kṛṇu deveṣu priyaṃ rājasu mā kṛṇu | priyaṃ sarvasya paśyata uta śūdra utārye ||
english: Make me dear among the gods, make me dear among kings. Make me dear in the sight of all who look — both the Śūdra and the Ārya.

sanskrit: ūdhnā vana hṛdā vana mukhena jihvayā vana | prapīnā payasā vana ||
english: Be pleased with the udder, be pleased with the heart, be pleased with the mouth and the tongue. Be pleased, O cow swollen full with milk.

sanskrit: vāñcha pado vāñcha tvacaṃ vāñchākṣyau vāñcha sakthyau | vatsam anu pra te mano nimnaṃ vār iva dhāvatu ||
english: Long for the foot, long for the hide, long for the eyes, long for the haunches. Let your mind flow toward the calf like water flowing downhill.

sanskrit: ūrdhvāni te lomāni tiṣṭhantv akṣyau kāmena śuṣyatām | sam id vatsena gaur iva mudrā sureva pṛcyatām ||
english: Let your hairs stand erect, let your eyes wither with longing. As the cow unites with the calf, as sura liquor is mixed — so let her be joined.

sanskrit: imā gāvaḥ sabandhavaḥ samānaṃ vatsam akrata | hiṅṅ iti karikratīr āddhārāniramavaśvasā ||
english: These cows, bound by kinship, have turned together toward one calf. Lowing with a hiṅ sound, performing their acts again and again, they stand full-uddered, drawing breath serenely.

sanskrit: śṛṅgaupaśā galabhūṣā aghnyāś carmavāsinīḥ | gāvo ghṛtasya mātaras tā vatsevā nayāmasi ||
english: Tasseled at the horns, adorned at the throat, inviolable, clad in their hides — the cows, mothers of ghee: we lead them as one leads calves.
